successors.name: Spanish Empire
successors.text: the Muisca land of Boyacá and Cundinamarca: the confederations of Bogotá (Bacatá), Tunja (Hunza), Sogamoso and Duitama

ledger.x: c. 800: the Muisca of the Altiplano Cundiboyacense (infobox 'c. 800-1540'; Early Muisca 800-1200, Late Muisca 1200-1537 in the page's period table). The page gives no date for when the confederations formed and the dates conflict (current consensus puts the Herrera period at 400 BCE-1000 CE).
20 April 1537: Jiménez de Quesada beats the zipa Tisquesusa at Funza.
Late August or early September 1537: the Spanish reach Sogamoso.
1538: Bacatá, the Bogotá savanna, passes to the Spanish with the founding of Bogotá on 6 August 1538 ('Bogotá founded August 6, 1538').
1539: Hunza, the Tunja country, passes to the Spanish with the founding of Tunja on 6 August 1539.
December 1539: Sogamoso and Duitama (Tundama) pass to the Spanish.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of the Muisca
wars.outcome: Spanish victory under Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada: Funza (20 Apr 1537), Hunza (20 Aug 1537), Sogamoso (Aug/Sep 1537), Bogotá founded 6 Aug 1538, Tunja founded 6 Aug 1539, Tundama defeated 15 Dec 1539; the last zaque executed early 1540.

wars.name: Muisca-Panche wars and the Battle of Tocarema
wars.outcome: Frequent warfare; the Muisca were beaten at the Battle of Tocarema (undated on the Confederation page); the conquest page dates Tocarema 20 August 1538 with the Spanish and Sagipa defeating the Panche.

certainty.note: Power rested 'on recognition of authorities, sometimes several at once, rather than strict subordination'.
The conquest is dated by town (Funza, Hunza, Sogamoso, Bogotá, Tunja, Duitama); the zone limits are discs.
